Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production pixel-art walk-cycle sprite sheet for Unity.
Input image 1 is the character identity and pixel-style reference atlas. Select ONLY the FIRST zombie, TOP-LEFT: lime-green stitched Frankenstein-like zombie, flat dark navy hair, torn blue jacket, slate undershirt, ripped brown trousers and brown boots. Preserve this exact character identity, clothing, body proportions and dark outlines.
Create ONE transparent PNG atlas showing EIGHT DISTINCT consecutive frames of this SAME zombie walking toward the viewer, fixed frontal camera. Grid EXACTLY 4 columns by 2 rows, equal cells, row-major animation order 1,2,3,4 / 5,6,7,8. Canvas landscape 1536x1024 if possible. Each cell is 384x512 with the character centered at x=192, planted ground baseline y=464. Whole body inside each cell, generous transparent margin, same body scale in all frames, no shadows on ground.
Frame choreography: 1 left foot forward contact/right arm forward; 2 weight drops onto left foot, rear heel rises; 3 right knee passing forward, arms passing mid-swing; 4 right leg extends forward, slight body rise; 5 right foot forward contact/left arm forward; 6 weight drops onto right foot, left heel rises; 7 left knee passing forward, arms passing mid-swing; 8 left leg extends, leading seamlessly to frame 1. Alternate leg silhouettes and counter-swing of both arms must be visibly different in all eight frames; do not repeat the same stance. Feet stay at consistent ground baseline when planted; head height moves only 1-2 logical pixels. Do NOT rotate to side view, mirror the asymmetric clothing, change identity or scale between frames.
Style: crisp chunky 16-bit pixel art matching input, consistent logical pixel size, very dark navy contours, limited palette and hard pixel clusters, 2-3 tones per material. Genuine transparent background and transparent gutters, no labels, numerals, borders, text, checkerboard drawing, environment, blur, antialiasing or motion streaks. Deliver the actual sprite atlas, not a mockup.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: Unity pixel-art animation atlas.

Draw EIGHT DISTINCT consecutive poses of this same character in a seamless normal dragging zombie walk, facing directly toward the viewer. Fixed camera, no rotation, no facing left/right.
EXACT grid 4 columns x 2 rows, 8 equal 384x512 cells on a 1536x1024 PNG. Read order top row 1-4 then bottom row 5-8. Same scale, center and ground baseline inside EVERY cell. Each full body entirely inside its own cell with at least 24px transparent padding; planted sole baseline at local y=464, body center x=192.

Frames 1 and 5 MUST show opposite legs forward. Each limb pose must actually change, not just shift or resize the whole sprite. Clothes follow the limbs consistently; do not mirror clothing, change face or add accessories. Minimal 1-2 logical pixel vertical bob.
Crisp chunky 16-bit pixel art matching reference, very dark navy outlines, limited palette, hard pixel clusters. Game sprite sheet only.
BACKGROUND MUST BE COMPLETELY EMPTY TRANSPARENCY: true RGBA alpha=0 everywhere outside each zombie, including gutters and holes between limbs. Character solid, no shadows or glow outside silhouettes, no gray/white backing, no vignette, no fake checkerboard, no gradients, no text, numbers, frames, ground or presentation mockup.

firstSheetBackgroundCorrection: Use case: background-extraction. Edit target: the provided 4x2 zombie sprite sheet. Remove the ENTIRE white/gray background AND every soft cast shadow around the sprites. Deliver a real transparent RGBA PNG: every background pixel must have alpha exactly ZERO, including corners, spaces inside legs, gutters and between fingers. The zombie art itself must be opaque with alpha 255. No semitransparent white veil. No white or gray canvas, no checkerboard painted into the image. Keep all eight existing zombie poses, all character colors, their positions, grid, dimensions 1536x1024 and pixel-art edges exactly as they are. Only remove background and diffuse shadows. Hard pixel silhouette, no soft halo. Actual game sprite sheet with empty transparency, not a presentation on paper.
